newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANY HEADS BIDS FOR 2006 WORLD CUP, SAYS FIFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY HEADS BIDS FOR 2006 WORLD CUP, SAYS FIFA.

text.p: World soccer chief Sepp Blatter said on Sunday that Germany is heading the list of bids to host the 2006 World Cup at the moment -- but it can expect fierce competition from across the world.
The Germans, who are involved in a battle with England to get the support of European governing body UEFA, were the first country to put forward their candidature for the finals in 1993.
Speaking in an interview on German television, FIFA general secretary Blatter said: "Germany is a very good candidate. There is no doubt about that. It was the first country to put its bid into FIFA.
"That counts at the moment because it is down as number one. But when it comes down to deciding the venue, it is the FIFA executive board who decide. All countries have a right to make a bid."
UEFA, keen to put all of its support behind just one country from Europe, will decide on April 17 whether to back Germany or England.
FIFA will decide on the venue in the year 2000.
Blatter made it clear that FIFA did not require UEFA to back just one candidate. Even if rejected by the European body, England would be able to continue their bid.

"The FIFA rules at the moment do not require a continent to put forward just one candidate," he said. "The Africans are coming with Morocco, Egypt and South Africa. South America has not held the event for a long time. There is Brazil, Argentina. (But) Germany is in a good position."
